HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. The reality behind the myth, the reveal shot. Under the new crooked stone bridge at night, one lantern hanging from the bridge's underside. The 'goblins' are real people, copied exactly from the attached human boards. Three grinning orphan boys in patched brown and white clothes with their purple, white and red goblin masks pushed back on cords round their necks, mouths full of rice cakes. A one-eyed old stonecutter with a long white beard and a mud-stained robe hems frayed to strips, leaning on his staff. A young mother with a heap of rags and stones bound on her head and a real baby on her back, wiping her hands. In the middle, the young madman Yongsu, sleeves tied back, counting silver into their palms from a wax tablet of sums. Warm lantern key from above, stone and water dropping to black around them, wet highlights as bokeh. A secret family, caught. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = yongsu. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: ch_rascals (the real people behind the goblin legend: copy each person's exact face, costume and props), ch_old_man_tree (the real people behind the goblin legend: copy each person's exact face, costume and props), ch_rock_lady (the real people behind the goblin legend: copy each person's exact face, costume and props), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), jougwan feather-cap board (shape only, ignore labels). BIHYUNG Colour #6a7cb0. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
